title: Object Storage Semantics: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Object Storage Semantics: Visual Guide

1. Not A File System | six operations compared side by side on a file system and an object store, from in-place byte writes to permission inheritance | an object store is an immutable key-value namespace with whole-object operations and prefix enumeration, so rename is copy-then-delete and there are no real directories

2. Listing Is Not Membership | a 1,000-object batch with a slider for when a reader lists, compared against a _SUCCESS marker and a manifest | a prefix listing observes upload progress rather than table membership, and only a manifest names the exact committed file set

3. One Key, Many Keys | a compactor replacing files A and B with C in three orders, showing what a reader sees at every intermediate step | strong per-key consistency does not make a group of puts and deletes atomic, so delete-first exposes missing rows and put-first exposes duplicates

4. Moving A Pointer Safely | two writers racing on current.json with an unconditional put and with a conditional if-match put, plus object locks and clock ordering | a conditional write on an etag or generation is compare-and-swap, and an unconditional overwrite loses an update while every operation returns success

5. Five Places To Crash | five failure windows in the publication protocol, each checked for reader consistency, idempotent recovery and safe cleanup | a lost commit acknowledgement is genuinely ambiguous so recovery must read the pointer first, and garbage collection needs a safety delay because pre-commit uploads look exactly like orphans
